Hi all — quick technical notes from my side so the session can be targeted: 

- SDKs: We support official SDKs (Python, Node). For telemetry ingestion at scale, Python async + connection pooling or Node streaming clients are common.
- Streaming patterns: chunked HTTP (SSE-like) for short-lived streams; persistent websocket or gRPC-based adapters for long-lived high-throughput pipelines. We'll demo the SDK streaming client using a simulated telemetry feed.
- Backpressure & batching: Recommend publisher-side batching windows (50–200ms) and a small buffer in-flight. Redwood's continuous batching reduces per-token cost while keeping latency within your SLO.
- Function/tool calling: Use strict JSON schema for tools that write to EHRs; implement a two-phase commit pattern (dry-run -> validate -> commit) in the demo to show safe failover.
- Security/connectivity: If you can share CIDRs or an SSO IP allowlist, Ben and I will validate firewall/egress and provide exact IPs and FQDNs.

Can someone share an approximate average prompt length (tokens) and a sample rate (msgs/sec) for typical telemetry so we can tune the demo? I attached a tiny CSV with sample telemetry profiles for reference.
